Subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization & migration - next steps

Hi Tom / Priya 

Great chat today, thanks for walking through your search/recs workflow and the migration constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of needs from your side:
- Migrate ~15M docs from current provider (one-off export available)
- Need parity for semantic search + kNN reranking and a vector DB backfill path
- Prefer 1536-dim embeddings today; open to testing 768 if cost/latency tradeoffs look good
- Tight latency SLO for online reranks (~50ms p95) which implies batching and KV cache considerations

Redwood follow-ups / ask list (next week):
1) You to share a small sample export (10k rows) with text + metadata and one example query set - this will let us run normalization/batching experiments (attachment placeholder).
2) We'll produce a short migration playbook covering: export format, backfill throughput, throttling knobs, and index consistency checks (see attached playbook).
3) Technical deep-dive: 60m session with your infra + our SEs to validate auth, SDK setup, and routing for canary traffic. Proposed times: Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13.
4) POC plan: start with 10k documents -> evaluate 1536 vs 768 dims for cosine vs dot-product scoring, test batch sizes (16/64/256) and normalization strategies.

Immediate asks from you before the deep-dive:
- Confirm the sample export and a point-of-contact for SSO/KMS requirements
- Any existing constraints on tokenization or chunking you currently apply

Attachments: acme-embeddings-sample.ndjson (sample export stub), redwood-embeddings-migration-playbook.pdf (migration checklist)

Thanks — I'll loop Rishi and Ethan on the technical session once we lock a time.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization & migration - next steps

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a 10k sample export (see acme-embeddings-sample.ndjson) and a short doc answering the items below. Quick answers inline: 

- Current provider: EmbedsCo using 1536-dim vectors, stored un-normalized; we use cosine similarity in the app (post-normalized in-service).
- We do chunk at 512 tokens with overlap for long documents.
- Point-of-contact for infra/SSO: Priya Nambiar (cc'd). For KMS we have a managed AWS KMS key.
- Would like to maintain identical rank ordering post-migration (or be able to tune to match).

Regarding batching: the online rerank is currently single-request per query with a batching buffer at the API gateway; we're open to Redwood's batching suggestions if it preserves p95 latency.

We can do the deep-dive on Wed 8/12 at 10:00 PT. Priya, can you confirm?

Tom
Head of Search, Acme AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priya Nambiar <priya@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization & migration - next steps

Hi all — looping in a few technical notes ahead of tomorrow's deep-dive. A couple quick points we'll validate during the session: 

1) Normalization: Redwood can accept un-normalized vectors and apply L2 normalization server-side (recommended when switching between providers). For exact rank reproducibility we'll run a small A/B comparing client-side vs server-side normalization on your sample set.

2) Dimensions & scoring: 1536 -> 768 is a common optimization but can change rank order. We'll produce a delta matrix for your query set (precision@k) so you can decide. If you require exact ordering, we'll tune the reranker and use model ensembling for edge cases.

3) Batching: for online rerank we typically recommend micro-batching (16-64) with async KV cache lookups to keep p95 under 60ms on our Dedicated configs. We'll instrument per-route tracing so you can see per-token latency.

4) Migration/backfill: we suggest an incremental backfill with a checkpointed worker and a per-shard concurrency cap (we'll include a sample backfill script in the playbook). We can throttle to avoid index contention.

I'll bring workload profiling scripts and a sample backfill snippet to the call. See you Wed 10:00 PT.

-rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
